title: A Classification of Translation-Invariant Quantum Codes in Any Dimension
abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes with two-dimensional translation invariance are known to be equivalent to copies of the two-dimensional toric code. Such a simple classification is not possible for quantum codes with higher dimensional translation invariance due to the existence of multiple types of toric codes and infinite families of fracton codes. Here, we focus on D-dimensional translation-invariant quantum codes based on length-D chain complexes. This includes multivariate multicycle codes where the number of variables equals the number of cycles. We show that such codes are equivalent to copies of D-dimensional toric codes. This directly generalizes the classification result for two-dimensional translation-invariant codes.
summary: This paper provides a rigorous mathematical classification of a specific class of quantum error-correcting codes (DDTI codes) in arbitrary dimensions. By utilizing tools from homological algebra, the authors prove that these codes are structurally equivalent to copies of the D-dimensional toric code. This result significantly generalizes existing knowledge in the field of topological quantum computation.
main_problem: To classify D-dimensional translation-invariant quantum codes (DDTI codes) based on their underlying mathematical structure derived from length-D chain complexes.
main_result: The authors prove that such codes are equivalent to copies of D-dimensional toric codes, generalizing the known 2D classification result.
method: The classification relies on advanced concepts from homological algebra, specifically analyzing CSS chain complexes and free resolutions of modules over the Laurent polynomial ring R = F_2[x_1, ..., x_D].
model_or_system: The system is quantum error-correcting codes defined on the infinite D-dimensional hypercubic lattice (Z^D), characterized by their stabilizer structure derived from chain complexes.
key_observables: The code Hamiltonian, the dimension k of the module M (determining the number of independent charge sectors), and the equivalence class of the code structure.
important_parameters: The dimensionality D of the lattice and the code, and the length of the underlying chain complex.
main_assumptions: The classification is restricted to DDTI codes derived from length-D chain complexes, excluding fractal codes. The result holds up to finite coarse-graining and local unitaries.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the main result: any DDTI qLDPC code based on a length-D chain complex satisfying the theorem is equivalent to copies of D-dimensional toric codes (TC).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the mathematical framework using homological algebra (resolutions, chain complexes) to prove structural theorems (e.g., equivalence of resolutions) which are then applied to classify the physical quantum codes.
why_interesting: While highly mathematical, the classification of topological quantum codes is fundamental to understanding fault-tolerant quantum computation, providing concrete structural results for realizing robust quantum memory.
